diagram_candidates.rationale: The counterexample is built from two explicit deterministic paths whose endpoint values agree while their path-space laws alternate; a small plot can make that distinction immediate.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Plot t on [0,1] horizontally and the e-direction coefficient vertically. Draw w_{2r}(t)=0 as the baseline and w_{2r+1}(t)=sin(πt)e as an arch with value 1 at t=1/2; mark both endpoints at 0 and show evaluation at t=1 sending both paths to 0. Label the path-space sup distance as 1. Keep it illustrative, not part of the proof.

diagram_candidates.kind: two-dimensional nested-cone and Fisher-metric projection schematic
diagram_candidates.rationale: The statement compares the full and null local cones and expresses the limit as a difference of squared distances from one Gaussian score point; this geometric relationship is easier to see in a labeled schematic.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: In illustrative two-dimensional coordinates, draw closed convex cones C₀⊂C from the origin, a point z=I⁻¹Z, and nearest points in each cone under the Fisher metric. Label d_I(z,C₀) and d_I(z,C), and annotate T∞=d_I²(z,C₀)−d_I²(z,C)≥0. Optionally show the linear map h↦I^(1/2)h that turns Fisher-distance ellipses into Euclidean circles. Label as a schematic, since d and the cones are general; do not imply the diagram proves local convergence or the limit theorem.
